subject: [RFC PATCH 2/5] mm/page_alloc: count a merged buddy's pages under the merged type

2026-10-07.patch_summary: This patch updates the page allocation code to correctly count pages when a merged buddy is freed. When a free page is merged with a buddy of another type at pageblock order and above, the buddy's pages are moved from their original type to the new merged type in the free counts. This ensures that per-type free counts are accurate and prevents undercounting on allocation later.

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain expressed concern that the patch may cause overflow in systems where MAX_PAGE_ORDER is significantly higher than pageblock_order, potentially regressing performance due to TLB optimization issues.
reviews.raw_body:
MAX_PAGE_ORDER > pageblock_order confuses things so much : (

Sashiko raises something:
https://sashiko.dev/#/patchset/20261007021250.1665929-1-riel%40surriel.com

Although feels like it is exaggerating.

My concern is for systems with a high diff between MAX_PAGE_ORDER and
pageblock_order. So on arm64 systems with 64K pagesize but pageblock
size as 2M (and PMD size 512M), the pageblock order is 5. We use this
configuration to reliably get TLB optimization from contpte size mappings.

Will we then repeatedly overflow the pcpu counter into the zone counter,
regressing stuff?

Perhaps I am overthinking. Your approach is clean, but perhaps we could
also do:

void account_freepages_move(zone, order, buddy_mt, mt)

	/* PCP-types do not have per-migratetype free counts. */
	if (likely (buddy_mt < MIGRATE_PCPTYPES && mt < MIGRATE_PCPTYPES))
		return;

account_freepages(zone, -(1 << order), buddy_mt);
account_freepages(zone, 1 << order, migratetype);

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary:
Author proposes a simple fix to reorder operations and avoid a potential underflow in the free page count by incrementing the merged type before decrementing the buddy's type.

Author acknowledged that per_cpu_pages struct does not keep counts on a per migratetype basis, and questioned the reviewer's concern about it.

Author acknowledged that the patch would throw off free counts when merging pages of different types, and explained that the current test only covers a subset of cases.
sentiment_signals: explained limitations of the current approach
reviews.raw_body:
I suppose if we switch the two lines around, doing
the increment on migratetype before decrementing
buddy_mt we could avoid that transient underflow?

---

The per_cpu_pages struct does not seem to keep
counts on a per migratetype basis at all. It
has per migratetype lists, but only one
pcp->count.

Also doesn't the pcp only carry order zero
pages currently?

I don't really understand your worry.

---

Wouldn't that throw off the counts when we merge
e.g. a MIGRATE_UNMOVABLE page with a MIGRATE_MOVABLE
buddy?

With your test we would only ever do the free count
adjustment for mismatched types if one of the pages
was HIGHATOMIC or CMA. That leaves the common case
without coverage.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Dev Jain noted that large deltas in __mod_zone_page_state can cause frequent overflows or underflows of pcp->vm_stat_diff, which defeats the purpose of per-cpu caching and may repeatedly trigger the if (unlikely(buddy_mt != migratetype)) branch.

Reviewer Dev Jain noted that since account_freepages() does not conditionally handle MOVABLE and UNMOVABLE types, the current patch's changes net to zero and suggested making it clear that this is only necessary for MIGRATE_PCPTYPES, unlike other types like MIGRATE_CMA and MIGRATE_HIGHATOMIC which have separate accounting.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry I was not talking about the pcp list (also, pcp carries
order 0 till 3?)

In __mod_zone_page_state, we use the per-cpu variable pcp->vm_stat_diff,
and when it overflows or underflows past a pcp->stat_threshold, we
push the diff to the global (zone) state.

The reason we do so is to optimize by batching zone operations into
per-cpu local operations.

My concern is that for large delta, we will always overflow
or underflow, defeating the purpose of the per-cpu caching.

So on said arm64 systems, we may frequently enter your

if (unlikely(buddy_mt != migratetype)

branch, and if pcp->stat_threshold is not enough, we may repeatedly
overflow and underflow, defeating this per-cpu optimization.

---

As you said, in account_freepages(), there is currently
no conditional based on MOVABLE and UNMOVABLE. So we
are essentially doing -x and +x, netting to zero.

So we could write my function, make it clear that currently
this is not needed for the MIGRATE_PCPTYPES, as opposed
to MIGRATE_CMA and MIGRATE_HIGHATOMIC which have separate
accounting.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author agreed that tracking migratetypes is necessary in the future, but deferred the change until later stages of the gigablock code development.
reviews.raw_body:
Lets defer this change until later.

During a later stage of the gigablock code, I
do need to track each zone's free pages by
migratetype, but it's not needed yet.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: reviewer suggested dropping an optimization in __free_one_page(), replacing it with direct calls to accounting add/del variants for improved simplicity and robustness
reviews.raw_body:
Reasonable on one hand, but I think at that point it would be simpler
and more robust to drop that 'single account_freepages() + __add/__del
operations' optimization, and just use the accounting add/del variants
directly instead.
